sources.entry: toolz - A collection of functional utilities for iterators, functions, and dictionaries. Also available as cytoolz for Cython-accelerated performance.

summary.one_liner: CyToolz is a Cython-compiled implementation of the toolz functional utilities library for iterables, functions, and dictionaries, offering the same API at higher speed.
summary.what_it_does: CyToolz implements the same API as the pure-Python toolz package, providing utility functions for iterables, functions, and dictionaries. The README says it is typically 2-5x faster than toolz, with a few larger gains. It is written in Cython and exposes a C API that other Cython projects can use. Functions are designed to work with built-in types like list and dict, and to return iterators where possible to keep memory use low. The README says it can process very large or infinite data sets. It is installed from PyPI and supports Python 3.9+. It also states experimental support for free-threaded Python 3.13 and provides wheels for that build.
use_cases: speed up functional data processing in python
process large or infinite iterators with low memory
compose and transform iterables and dictionaries
use functional utilities from a Cython project via C API
notable: Drop-in API match with pure-Python toolz
Typically 2-5x faster than toolz per README
Exposes a C API usable from other Cython projects
caveats: Free-threading support is experimental and not yet tested for thread-safety
